name: Estuary and Salmon Restoration Program

funder.name: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife

summary: Biennial grants for restoring and protecting near-shore habitat, estuaries and salmon habitat in Puget Sound, run as separate request-for-proposals tracks for restoration and protection, beach restoration small grants and regional pre-design.

amount.note: Limit for Restoration and Protection grants; other tracks have lower limits

reporting: Grantees must submit a stewardship plan that identifies how the site and restoration investment is to be protected over time, and restoration projects must be operated and maintained for 10 years after construction is completed.

status.quote: Full Applications and Portfolio Applications Due May 22, 2026

deadline.quote: Full Applications and Portfolio Applications Due May 22, 2026

status.quote: Final Applications Due in PRISM March 31, 2026

deadline.quote: Final Applications Due in PRISM March 31, 2026

administered_by.quote: This grant program is managed by the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife with RCO administering the grants.

applicant_types.quote: Who May Apply? Federal agencies Local agencies Native American Tribes Nonprofit organizations Private institutions State agencies Universities and colleges

geography.quote: All projects must be in Puget Sound, east of Cape Flattery.

access.quote: Each grant program issues its own Request for Proposal with a specific grant application and review process.

window.quote: Estuary and Salmon Restoration Program funding is awarded every two years.

co_finance_required.quote: Match is not required for any ESRP grant program in the 2026 grant round.

reporting.quote: Grant recipients must submit a stewardship plan that identifies how the site and restoration investment is to be protected over time. Restoration projects must be operated and maintained for 10 years after construction is completed.
